title: Article 104 — Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation under Article 99 or when not qualified or when disqualified

content.overview: Article 104 provides that if a person sits or votes as a member of either House of Parliament before complying with Article 99 (oath), or when he knows that he is not qualified or that he is disqualified for membership, or that he is prohibited from so doing by any law, he shall be liable in respect of each day on which he so sits or votes to a penalty of five hundred rupees to be recovered as a debt due to the Union.
content.glance: Sitting/voting without oath, or when unqualified/disqualified/prohibited → penalty ₹500 per day, recoverable as debt to Union.
content.study:
Article 104 is a deterrent against unauthorised participation. The penalty is ₹500 for each day of sitting or voting in breach, recoverable as a debt due to the Union.

Examination: triggers (no oath; known lack of qualification; known disqualification; legal prohibition); daily penalty; recovery as debt.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Sitting or voting as a member without Article 99 oath, or knowing of disqualification/non-qualification/prohibition → ₹500 per day, recoverable as debt due to the Union.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the penalty under Article 104?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 104, a person who sits or votes as a member of either House before making the Article 99 oath, or when he knows he is not qualified or is disqualified or prohibited by law from so doing, is liable to a penalty of five hundred rupees for each day on which he so sits or votes, recoverable as a debt due to the Union.

examTips: ₹500 per day for sitting/voting without oath or when disqualified.
